header_decisions: DEC-22 (SandboxBackend reversal; microVM provider) gates S7 and S8. S0 records the reversal in the ledger; the reversal itself needs owner approval (owner decision table, row 12).

DEC-23 (delegated user bearer, thread-only scope, 256 file / 64 MiB quota as DEC-23 D6, ZDR refusal as D8, retention and erasure) is recorded by S0 and implemented by S1-S5. It gates the S3 default flip, the S5 default-on (together with the WS17 thread-delete hook) and S8. Billed or persistent compute needs the Control decision model.thread.sandbox_workspace.
DEC-24 (no promote caller: the Space overlay is visible only to its own lease) is recorded by S4 as an honest limit.

S0-S6 need no decision beyond recording. Every WS22 switch defaults off: SANDBOX_MANAGER_THREAD_WORKSPACE (S1), EXECUTION_CORE_THREAD_WORKSPACE (S2), SANDBOX_THREAD_WORKSPACE_ENABLED (S3, BFF) and EXECUTION_CORE_SPACE_WORKSPACE_WRITE_THROUGH (S4).

slices.title: Thread-scope workspace sync in execution-core (flag off)
slices.summary: Adds the thread scope to execution-core: ensure_thread_lease (cached in StateStore by run_id, zdr false) and a workspace_sync module whose open hydrates the thread files into a fresh directory behind a Drop guard and whose commit uploads changes and deletions, reports conflicts and never overwrites them. The exclusion predicate skips the program file, scratch, .tmp, .mplconfig, __pycache__, attachments/ and files over 8 MiB. The runtime loop gets a thread branch that reports a workspace result, and ExecuteStepRequest.thread_id = 13 is used only for the workspace and never forwarded to memory tools. slices.title: BFF bearer, code_interpreter thread wiring and honest workspace field
slices.summary: Wires the thread workspace through the BFF and model-gateway. The BFF also mints the aud=sandbox-manager bearer for a non-ZDR personal turn when SANDBOX_THREAD_WORKSPACE_ENABLED is true, model-gateway's code_interpreter forwards thread_id into ExecuteStepRequest, and every code_interpreter result carries a workspace field with scope thread, space or ephemeral and state synced, conflict or refused. Ephemeral results state that files are not kept, and provenance stays unscreened. With no bearer the call degrades to ephemeral and says so; ZDR turns mint no bearer and send no thread id. sse.rs is verify-only.

slices.title: Thread workspace retention, erasure and user Reset
slices.summary: Adds retention and erasure for thread workspaces. A sweeper, modelled on the process sweeper, deletes workspaces idle past SANDBOX_MANAGER_THREAD_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30) and old lease rows. DeleteThreadWorkspace removes the rows first and then the cas/thread/<org>/<thread>/ blobs through a new Go S3 delete client in objectstore. The model-gateway gets GET and DELETE /v1/threads/{thread_id}/workspace (owner-bound), exposed through the BFF and the chat-workspace action contract (chat.workspace.list, chat.workspace.reset), with a Thread files and Reset control in the SPA. Gates the default-on together with the WS17 thread-delete hook.

slices.summary: Introduces a SandboxBackend trait in execution-core (id, profile, exec, spawn, health) with a BackendError that carries a SandboxFailureCause. BwrapBackend wraps the existing executor, a RemoteExecutorBackend client is added, code_interpreter, process_host and http_health call the trait, and MpSandboxPolicy::External routes to the remote backend. A new conformance suite pins the contract against a real executor stub. Behaviour is unchanged. Gated on DEC-22; the ledger trigger is a planned microVM backend.

slices.title: microVM sandbox spike ending in an ADR (gated DEC-22/23)
slices.summary: Time-boxed spike for a second attested executor and sandbox-manager pair with its own backend_id, idle-stop and encrypted snapshots. It ends in an ADR (number integrator-allocated; ADR-0009 is a placeholder) that decides the provider, region, cost, guest-image owner, patch and supply-chain duty, snapshot retention and destruction, VM-second metering with cost-core, and the Control decision (DEC-23 option b). Ships no code; any browser in the VM uses WS21 grants and Quarry executes.
